key_insight: Recourse policies must account for causal effects on both features and true outcomes, or they can accidentally encourage gaming instead of genuine improvement.
engineering_relevance: For high-stakes decision systems, causal recourse can improve stability, reduce distribution shift from strategic behavior, and lessen the need for frequent retraining.
method: Model recourse actions inside a structural causal model
Formulate recourse as a causal performative optimization problem
Use iterative dynamics to find performatively stable solutions
evidence_signal: Experiments on semi-synthetic and real credit datasets show the causal approach outperforms standard empirical risk minimization while reducing retraining needs under strategic behavior.
watch_item: The optimization becomes non-convex, so implementation may be sensitive to initialization, model specification, and causal assumptions.
paper_title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse
